LESSON: INTEGRATED FARMING

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 9
Subject: GRADE
Strand: Conservation of Resources
Topic 1.3: Integrated farming
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 12

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Integrated farming, part of Conservation of Resources in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 9 GRADE.

Key inquiry question: how components of integrated How can integrated farming conserve resources?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Integrated farming together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Creativity and imagination: Observation and making connection skills as learners seek information, design and make a

model to depict integrated farming enterprise.

• Critical thinking and problem solving: Evaluation and decision-making skills as learners analyse the environment for

components of integrated farming and design models of integrated farming enterprise.

Values:
• Unity: Team work as learners harness gifts and special skills of the group members in designing and making an integrated

farming model.

• Respect: Accommodating diverse opinions while learners discuss and design model of integrated farming.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Environmental awareness and protection as learners re-use locally available resources such as waste pieces of wood, cartons,

cardboards and papers to design and make a model of integrated farming enterprise.
